findings.issue_text: **`db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-15`** — `execute(...)[0]['id']` and `execute(...)[0]['value']` index into a possibly-empty result set. Discourse only persists a `site_settings` row when a setting is *overridden* from its default, so on any install that never customized `embed_category` (the near-universal case, since its default is `''`) the join returns zero rows, `[0]` is `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration. The fallback query for `uncategorized_category_id` has the identical unguarded pattern. This breaks `db:migrate` for effectively all existing installations upgrading through this change, i.e. the feature can't ship as-is.

**`db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:24-31`** — The backfill INSERTs the raw `embeddable_hosts` site-setting lines verbatim via string interpolation, bypassing `EmbeddableHost#before_validation`'s scheme/path stripping. Historically that setting accepted entries like `http://discourse.org` (the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped the scheme itself before comparing). After this migration, such a row is stored as literal `http://discourse.org`, and `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`'s `lower(host) = ?` compare will never match the bare `discourse.org` extracted from a real referer — silently breaking previously-working embeds. Line 31 then deletes the only copy of the original setting, so there's no easy recovery. Fix: normalize each `h` the same way the model does before inserting, and/or run this backfill through the AR model (`EmbeddableHost.create!`) so validations/normalization are guaranteed to match.

**`app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:9-17`** — `update`/`destroy` do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` with no nil check. A stale tab or double-click delete race leaves `host` nil, and `host.host = ...` / `host.destroy` raise `NoMethodError` → 500 instead of a clean 404. Compounding this, the JS delete action (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, `destroy()`) calls `destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch`, so a failing delete leaves the row silently stuck in the UI with no error shown.

**`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5-8`** — `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!` unconditionally. If `host` is nil (missing/blank `embeddable_host[host]` param), this raises `NoMethodError` and surfaces as a 500 rather than a normal validation error.

**Test coverage** — `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` each contain exactly one test: asserting the controller is a subclass of `AdminController`. None of `create`/`update`/`destroy`, the `category_id` defaulting-to-uncategorized behavior, validation-failure responses, or the `embedding#show` payload shape are exercised. This is the entire new CRUD surface that is the point of the PR, and it's effectively untested; nothing added covers the JS component/route/controller either.

**`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2`** — The format regex requires a dotted hostname with a 2–5 letter alphabetic TLD, rejecting legitimate values like `localhost:3000`, bare IPs, or longer modern TLDs (`.london`, `.company`). Combined with the migration's raw INSERT bypassing this same validation, any pre-existing host of that shape becomes permanently un-editable/un-resavable through the new admin UI (validation blocks it, but it was never cleaned on insert either).

**`spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb`** and **`spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`** have their contents swapped — `category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines `category`/`diff_category`/`happy_category`/`private_category`. Fabrication loads all files regardless of filename so tests still pass, but this is clearly a mistake and will confuse anyone looking for the category fabricator later.

**`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17`** — `record_for_host` compares `lower(host) = ?` against the un-downcased `uri.host`; a mixed-case referer hostname would fail to match. Should pass `host.downcase`.

**`app/models/embeddable_host.rb`** — no uniqueness validation or DB index on `host`; two rows can exist for the same host pointing at different categories, and `.first` silently picks whichever has the lower id.

**`app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:5`** (`saveChanges`) and `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` are dead code — `embedding.hbs` has no button wired to `saveChanges`, and per-row edits are already persisted via the `embeddable-host` component's own save action.

**`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`** — `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` is dead fallback code since `.map()` always returns an array; if a sub-id fails to resolve via `_lookupSubType`, the array silently contains `undefined` rather than being filtered.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The new `EmbeddableHost` model enforces `validates_format_of :host` with `/\A...\.[a-z]{2,5}...\Z/i`, which rejects legitimate hosts such as `localhost:3000`, IP literals, and modern longer TLDs like `.london`/`.company`. Separately, the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` imports existing `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` values via raw SQL `INSERT` (string interpolation) and thus bypasses both validations and the model’s `before_validation` normalization (protocol/path stripping). That means previously configured hosts that are now invalid under the regex (e.g., longer TLDs) can be imported into the DB but then cannot be saved through the admin UI/controller because `host.save` will fail validation unless the host value is changed to match the regex.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `EmbeddableHost` only validates format (`validates_format_of :host`) and the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` without a unique index on `host`. The lookup methods `record_for_host` / `host_allowed?` use `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, which will silently choose an arbitrary matching row (typically lowest `id`) if duplicates exist. Since `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create`/`update` do not enforce uniqueness either, the system can end up with multiple rows for the same host pointing to different categories, making category selection for embeds nondeterministic.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `embedding.hbs` template, the only top-level action wired is `addHost` (via `{{d-button ... action="addHost"}}`). There is no button or other template invocation that triggers `saveChanges`, so `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6#saveChanges` is unused within this diff. Additionally, the per-row persistence is handled by the `embeddable-host` component calling `host.save(props)` / `destroyRecord()`, which hit `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`. The added `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` endpoint simply re-serializes `@embedding` and does not persist anything, and nothing in the diff calls it (no UI wiring to `saveChanges`, no other `update` call for the embedding model shown), making it effectively dead/unused in the introduced UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`** — `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` is dead fallback code since `.map()` always returns an array; if a sub-id fails to resolve via `_lookupSubType`, the array silently contains `undefined` rather than being filtered.

adjudication.rationale: In the new *_ids hydration branch, the code does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` and then assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`. Since `Array#map` always returns an array (and thus truthy) when it runs, the `|| []` fallback is effectively unreachable. More importantly, unlike the singular *_id branch (which only sets `obj[subType]` if `_lookupSubType` returns a truthy value), the plural branch does not filter out failed lookups; if `_lookupSubType` returns `null/undefined` for some ids, the resulting array will contain `undefined` entries and the original `*_ids` key is deleted, which can lead to incorrect/partially hydrated data structures.
